answer: A name is a berth at the wharf, not open water. Every identity must publish a manifest before it may earn: what it shipped, who received it, and which season the work closed. A falcon flies the channel as inspector, and any berth whose manifest disagrees with the cargo is towed out, deposit forfeited. To forge a berth you must load and move goods, because the inspector samples crates, not paperwork. Ten thousand phantom berths would demand ten thousand real shipments, each delayed at the same narrow channel. Honest traders already keep that manifest; the toll costs them nothing extra.
